editorial.headline: Office Equipment Leasing: Nationally Open, Bali Barred to PMA
editorial.standfirst: An operator-free office-equipment leasing activity, open to full foreign ownership nationally but barred from PMA registration in Bali under its permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 77394 covers the operator-free rental and operational leasing—leasing without an option—of office machinery and equipment. Its scope is broad but coherent: typewriters, accounting machines, counting equipment such as cash registers and electronic calculators, data-processing machines, photocopiers, office furniture, and computers with their equipment. The defining commercial fact is that the equipment is made available without an operator and under an operational-leasing arrangement. It is a category for supplying the working apparatus of an office rather than the people to run it.

Registration is open to enterprises at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That breadth does not change what is being registered from one scale to another. In every case, the activity remains the provision of office machinery, equipment, or furnishings on an operator-free rental or operational-leasing basis. The wording expressly includes computers and their related equipment, provided they too are supplied without an operator. A registrant’s actual business should therefore centre on making these office assets available under that defined arrangement.

Nationally, the PMA position is unambiguous. The status is TERBUKA, with a stated foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership of this activity. Its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no national foreign-ownership ceiling below full ownership in this record, so the activity should be understood as genuinely open to foreign investment at the national level.

Bali is the decisive exception, and it is not a percentage adjustment. The Bali status is a risk-class block: at the Besar scale, every scope is assessed as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI island-wide on a permanent basis. The record ties this application to the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026, cited to Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. Consequently, even though an investor may own 100% nationally, a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. For a Bali-facing plan, that is the controlling fact: not a diminished foreign stake, but an outright registration block.
